items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: that was the first one that I flew to New York to do with Kenny Barron and whoever it was, Ron Carter and Ben Riley.

ctx.x: I can hear him say that.

Yeah. “Jamey, that’s the hardest thing I’ve ever had to do.” I said, “What’s that?” He said, “Just to comp for five minutes like that.” But yes, so on some of those early ones I would scat sing. I’d have a microphone you know [scats]. And that seemed to free up the piano player. And if you listen on that Volume Six behind you there, if you listen carefully you can hear me playing the alto because that was my sixth play-a-long and that was the first one that I flew to New York to do with Kenny Barron and whoever…
Well I can see how the keyboardist and the bass player could not intentionally but sort of zone out after a while.

items.title: Aebersold Jamey — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: They were all really nice to work with in the studio.

ctx.x: Yeah, basically. But some of them are really slowed down. If you have, like, my CD player here, which goes up or down a whole step, but as you go up, it speeds up, and as you go down, it slows down. As you go up, it kind of sounds weird, and as you go down, it sounds weird. But his program doesn’t allow for any of that. Everything still sounds authentic, but slower tempos.
Let me ask you this. I was just looking at the musicians. Come Volume 6, Charlie Parker, you’ve got Kenny Barron, Ron Carter and Ben Riley.
